name: Tessera Industries Anti-Material Beam AMB-2 'Eraser'
description: A crew-served directed energy weapon that fires a sustained coherent particle beam capable of ablating solid matter at the molecular level. The AMB-2 does not burn, explode, or impact — it disassembles the target material one molecular layer at a time, converting solid matter into a fine dust that disperses on the wind. Against vehicle armor, the beam carves through plating like an invisible saw. Against structures, it cuts clean holes with mirror-smooth edges. Against biological targets, the effect is so rapid that the nervous system does not have time to register pain before the affected tissue simply ceases to exist. Tessera developed it for precision demolition of contaminated structures, and its military applications are a source of ongoing internal corporate debate.
specifications:
beam type: Coherent particle beam
effective range: 20-300 meters
abalation rate: 2mm of hardened steel per second of sustained exposure
power source: Vehicle-mounted fusion generator
beam diameter: 5 cm focused
weight: 120 kg on tripod (plus generator)
crew: 2 operators
continuous operation: 60 seconds before emitter cooling required
cooling period: 90 seconds
story_hooks: A building wall was cut open with mirror-smooth edges in a perfect rectangle — nothing in the conventional weapons catalog makes cuts like that, but a Tessera AMB-2 does.

A Tessera engineer has leaked that the AMB-2's particle beam has an unintended secondary effect — the molecular dust it produces is carcinogenic, and contamination zones around test sites are making people sick years later.

physical_description.visual_profile: A imposing, industrial directed-energy cannon resembling a hybrid between a particle accelerator and a precision surgical instrument. The weapon presents a stark, engineered silhouette with minimal ornamentation — all function, no flourish. The barrel assembly dominates the profile, a long tapered column that seems to taper toward an almost invisible aperture.
physical_description.dimensions: Main assembly: 185cm length, 45cm width at mount base, 110cm height on tripod. Barrel taper section: 120cm. Beam aperture: 5cm diameter.
physical_description.weight_description: Massively hefty — requires vehicle mounting or permanent emplacement. The tripod alone feels anchored to the earth; the gun itself resists casual handling with its distributed mass across the massive fusion capacitor core.
physical_description.primary_material: Brushed titanium-composite frame with embedded superconductor channels visible beneath transparent thermal-shielding panels. The barrel is a layered assembly of high-density ceramic and magnetized ferro-alloy.
physical_description.finish: Industrial matte gunmetal with sectional anodized panels in deep charcoal. Thermal-dissipation fins along the emitter neck show a polished, mirror-smooth surface. Wear patterns and scorch marks from repeated firing cycles visible around the barrel aperture.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary, charcoal black accents, with cobalt-blue luminescent coolant visible through reinforced viewport ports. Tessera Industries' corporate silver badge contrasts against the dark palette.
physical_description.grip_texture: Twin reinforced handles wrapped in rubberized polymer with integrated capacitive contact pads for power distribution and targeting. Non-slip, heat-resistant coating shows micro-abrasion from gloved operator hands.
distinctive_features: Translucent thermal-monitoring viewport running the length of the emitter column, glowing faint blue with circulating coolant
Array of status LEDs (amber, red, green) clustered at the rear junction box indicating power state, thermal load, and targeting lock
Fine particulate exhaust vents along the barrel taper, designed to safely disperse ablated matter
Precision crosshair reticle marking visible on the minimal aperture opening
Angular heat-sink fins flared asymmetrically around the focusing coil — engineered for active thermal management
Cable conduit running from the weapon body to external fusion generator, shielded in reinforced armored flex-cable
Scorch and micro-ablation marks radiating outward from the barrel aperture — evidence of weapons testing
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Tessera Industries corporate logo (stylized geometric hourglass) stamped on the left thermal panel in brushed silver. Serial number and testing classification (TESSERA/MIL-CLASS-5/TEST) etched in small font on the junction box. Red warning placards with radioactive and directed-energy symbols mounted on the tripod base.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but combat-worn. The weapon shows evidence of rigorous testing — the barrel aperture has micro-scarring patterns from repeated molecular-level discharge events, and the thermal vents display oxidized residue from dispersed ablated materials. No visible rust or corrosion, suggesting meticulous maintenance protocols. The finish retains its industrial integrity despite obvious field deployment.
